To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the humoral immune responses are significantly depressed in hyperinsulinaemic alloxan diabetic animals.

the immune response is depressed in alloxan-induced diabetic mice, that this effect is not caused by the excess of corticoid hormones and that the impaired response is probably related to a decreased activity of insulin receptors on lymphocytes.
the impaired humoral response in alloxan diabetes is due to a decreased function of B-lymphocytes and possibly also of T-helper cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of alloxan-induced diabetes in the immune responses.
the effect of alloxan diabetes on the immune response.
the effects of alloxan diabetes on the immune system in mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diabetes per se does not impair the immune response but rather the insulin deficiency which is a consequence of the diabetic state.

the impaired immune function in diabetic animals is due to a combination of factors including hyperglycaemia, hypoinsulinaemic state, glucosuria, ketonuria, hyperlipidaemia, hypercorticosteroidism and possibly also other metabolic abnormalities which are not yet identified. the immune system in diabetes mellitus may be affected in a number of different ways, and that the impairment of the immune response may depend on the degree and duration of the disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the humoral immunity of alloxan diabetic mouse is impaired and that it is not the result of hyperglycaemia or corticosteroid excess.
hyperglycaemia is a significant factor in the impairment of immune response in diabetes.
diabetes in mice, as in man, may be a disease of impaired immune responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system is impaired in diabetes, and that this impairment is due to the hyperglycemia.
hyperglycemia is not the sole reason for the immune deficiency in diabetes, but it is a contributing factor.
hyperglycemia is not a major factor in the immunosuppression of alloxan diabetic BALC/C mice.
